cases.import_capacity_note: Strongly interconnected with the Nordic market and by subsea cables to Great Britain and Germany (among others). In 2022 the cables mostly ran as net export routes toward high-priced continental and UK markets, e.g. a 663 GWh net export in week 9 of 2022.

warning.what: End of week 9 2022: NO2 reservoir filling 34.4% vs a 2002-2021 median of 52.2% (-17.8 pp); national 37.0% vs 46.1%; NO5 27.2% vs 39.4%
warning.basis: From the NVE week-9 report (early March 2022) to the NO2 record daily price on 18 Aug 2022

actions.description: Authorities asked hydro producers to save water and refill reservoirs ahead of winter, instead of producing and exporting at high prices. In July 2022 the minister said measures to limit water use for generation and/or exports could not be ruled out, and NVE asked producers to save water for winter generation.
actions.lead_time_basis: Voluntary request; no formal start date found
actions.cost_note: No cost estimate found; the industry (Energi Norge) warned that holding too much water could cause spillage later
actions.effect: Reservoirs not quantified in the sources read. NVE called rationing 'very unlikely' by 20 Sep 2022.

actions.description: Export-limitation / 'security of supply' mechanism. The government prepared rules putting reservoir refilling ahead of generation and exports when seasonal reservoir levels are unusually low. Producers had to report reservoir levels (reporting scheme introduced in 2022). A later bill made producers formally responsible for keeping reservoirs above a level, and exports could be restricted at very low levels.
actions.lead_time_basis: Announced Aug 2022 and 'not expected until early next year'; the formalising bill came later (Zawya/Reuters, undated, says it formalised procedures 'introduced the previous year')
actions.cost_note: Neighbouring Nordic countries criticised it as power protectionism
actions.effect: No export restriction was triggered in 2022 according to the sources read; the mechanism acts as a backstop

actions.description: Household electricity support (stromstotte): the state paid a share of the spot price above 70 ore/kWh (80% in summer months, 90% otherwise in 2022; later 90% all year). This shields consumers from the price signal, so it is the opposite of a conservation tariff.
actions.lead_time_basis: Scheme already running in 2022; start date not confirmed in sources read
actions.cost_note: About NOK 32.6 bn paid to households in 2022, the largest month being December 2022 at about NOK 8.5 bn. Not converted to USD because no sourced exchange rate was read.
actions.effect: Bill relief; no measured demand effect in the sources read

outcome.blackout_or_shedding: None. Statnett put the chance of winter rationing at 5-20% (July 2022); NVE called rationing 'very unlikely' (Sep 2022). NO2 hit a record daily price of EUR 532.52/MWh for 18 Aug 2022; summer retail-area prices were just over NOK 3/kWh in July 2022.
outcome.what_worked: Very large reservoir storage plus import capacity gave time; saving water over the summer and the threat of export controls kept reservoirs from running out before spring.
outcome.what_failed: The price spike passed straight to consumers in the south, and an expensive universal subsidy (about NOK 32.6 bn in 2022) followed; the export-control idea caused friction with neighbours.

cases.summary: A record heatwave and Yangtze-basin drought in July-August 2022 halved Sichuan's hydro reservoirs while peak load rose 25% y/y; the province suspended power to industrial users from 15 August, cut lighting and commercial hours, imported power via State Grid and tried cloud seeding. Supply to general industry resumed on 28 August when rain and cooler weather arrived.

hydro_share_pct.note: over 80% of provincial generation; Sichuan produces ~30% of China's hydro output and normally exports nearly a third of its generation east via UHV

cases.storage_note: Large cascade reservoirs but much run-of-river capacity; reservoir water levels fell by as much as half in August 2022 and some major plants 'bottomed out', halving provincial hydro capacity.
cases.enso_note: 2022 was a La Nina year; sources read attribute the event to heat and drought without an explicit ENSO link.
cases.import_capacity_note: Sichuan is normally a large exporter over UHV lines to Shanghai, Zhejiang and Jiangsu; State Grid delivered about 130 GWh/day into Sichuan during the crisis, and State Grid and Southern Grid reported moving power from 15 provinces.

warning.what: Yangtze-basin rainfall 30% below normal in July (60% below in August); crisis declared from 7 August
warning.basis: July rainfall deficit to the 7 Aug start of extreme heat/load and 15 Aug industrial cut-off

actions.description: Provincial order ('leave power for the people') suspended or curbed power to industrial plants: initial halt 15-20 August, later extended to 25 August; affected solar polysilicon (Tongwei, GCL), cement, urea, CATL, BOE, Foxconn; Chongqing applied similar curbs from 17 August.
actions.lead_time_basis: order issued 14 Aug and effective 15 Aug
actions.cost_note: More than a dozen listed firms warned of delivery delays and 'billions of yuan' in losses; no aggregate figure
actions.effect: Freed supply for residential cooling; residential demand peaked at 473 GWh/day on 27 Aug

actions.description: Rolling blackouts reached residential users; Dazhou announced rolling three-hour daily outages for neighbourhoods.
actions.lead_time_basis: applied within the August emergency
actions.effect: Not quantified

actions.description: State Grid delivered power into Sichuan from other provinces (reported transfers from 15 provinces by State Grid and Southern Grid), reversing the province's normal export role; exports east were cut.
actions.lead_time_basis: same month
actions.effect: About 130 GWh/day delivered into Sichuan

actions.description: Chengdu switched off outdoor advertising and landscape lighting and half-lit subway stations; malls and commercial venues (incl. Chongqing) shortened hours.
actions.lead_time_basis: mid-August measures
actions.effect: Not quantified

actions.description: Cloud seeding across Yangtze provinces (rockets/silver iodide in Hubei; 900 seeding rockets made available in Chongqing; drones reported in Sichuan) to induce rain for reservoirs and crops.
actions.lead_time_basis: mid-August operations
actions.effect: No measured effect; thin cloud cover stalled efforts in some areas

outcome.blackout_or_shedding: Industrial power suspended 15-~25 Aug 2022; residential rolling outages (e.g. 3 h/day in Dazhou); general industrial and commercial supply resumed by noon 28 Aug, except some energy-intensive plants
outcome.gdp_impact: No aggregate estimate found; Sichuan is ~4% of national industrial output and ~5% of GDP, but ~14% of China's PV and semiconductor wafer production, so supply-chain effects were wider (polysilicon, batteries, electronics)
outcome.what_worked: Hard prioritisation of residential load over industry kept households mostly supplied; inter-provincial transfers via State Grid (~130 GWh/day); rain and cooling from ~28 Aug restored hydro (daily hydro output back up to ~460 GWh).
outcome.what_failed: No reservoir reserve or demand-response market to handle a concurrent 25% peak-load surge and halved hydro; long-term export commitments to eastern provinces constrained local supply; cloud seeding had no demonstrable effect.

cases.source_notes: Extension to 25 Aug [7], Dazhou 3h outages and 15-province transfers [6], cloud seeding [4] and Bloomberg restoration [5] are from search-result extracts; Reuters/Tribune [0], Caixin [1], Yicai [2], Al Jazeera [3] were fetched. No GW shortfall figure or official economic-loss estimate was found. S&P Global piece returned 403.

cases.summary: Uruguay's worst drought in about a century cut hydro output in early 2023. UTE replaced it with costly thermal plants and, from Feb 2023, with cheap imports from Brazil. The large wind fleet built after the 2008 drought carried much of the load. No rationing was reported in the sources read.

hydro_share_pct.note: Share of demand met by hydro from 1 Jan to early Feb 2023 (drought), per ADME via El Observador; the normal-year share was not read. In 2008 hydro was about 40% of supply.

cases.storage_note: Salto Grande (binational with Argentina) and Rio Negro dams; limited storage, with the Rio Negro basin sharply depleted
cases.import_capacity_note: Brazil: up to 500 MW via the Melo-Candiota converter and 70 MW via Rivera; Argentina interconnected via Salto Grande

warning.what: Drought intensifying from late 2022
warning.basis: No dated early-warning metric found in the sources read

actions.description: Ran thermal plants including the Punta del Tigre combined cycle on gasoil and fuel oil; thermal supplied 28% of demand year to date by early Feb 2023
actions.lead_time_basis: Existing plants dispatched
actions.cost_note: About $60M of fuel from 1 Jan to early Feb 2023; about $1.5M/day; $193.5/MWh is the Punta del Tigre combined-cycle cost
actions.effect: Covered 28% of demand

actions.description: Imports from Brazil starting 4 Feb 2023: 498 MW flat each hour at $57.7/MWh (about $60/MWh later), replacing costlier thermal; also imports from Argentina
actions.lead_time_basis: Uses existing interconnection capacity
actions.cost_note: Saves roughly $136/MWh vs Punta del Tigre (estimate: 193.5 - 57.7)
actions.effect: On one day in Feb 2023, imports were over 50% of supply in the morning hours; 34% of 1,526 MW demand came from Brazil, 49% from wind and 7% from thermal

outcome.blackout_or_shedding: None reported in the sources read
outcome.what_worked: Diversification after 2008 (wind is about half of supply on some days) and interconnection with Brazil made a severe drought a cost problem, not a shortage. In 2008 the same kind of drought cost UTE about $1 bn extra and needed $200M of emergency generators bought without tender.
outcome.what_failed: Costly fuel-oil and gasoil thermal backup; financial strain on UTE

cases.summary: A heatwave and drought from early May 2023 drained northern hydro reservoirs below dead level just as several coal units failed, leaving the northern grid short by up to about 5 GW and forcing rolling cuts to homes and industrial parks in early-mid June. Rain in late June refilled reservoirs and cuts ended around 22 June; the World Bank put the preliminary cost at about USD 1.4bn (0.3% of GDP).

hydro_share_pct.note: share of northern-region supply as of May 2023 (VnExpress); nationally hydro supplies 'almost half' of energy needs per AFP/World Bank coverage

cases.storage_note: Large northern reservoirs (Son La, Lai Chau, Hoa Binh, Thac Ba, Tuyen Quang, Hua Na) but annual rather than multi-year; by 3 June several had only 0.4-0.9 days of water and Lai Chau and Son La were below dead storage level. Northern hydro output fell to 12-15% of supply, about half the prior year's level.
cases.enso_note: 2023 El Nino onset coincided; sources read attribute the crisis to heat and drought, not explicitly to ENSO.
cases.import_capacity_note: Imports from China and Laos supplied only 10-12 GWh/day (2.7% of northern daily demand). The single 500kV north-south backbone was limited to about 2,200-2,500 MW of transfer to the north.

warning.what: EVN forecast in April a northern summer shortfall of 1,600-4,900 MW
warning.basis: April 2023 EVN forecast to the start of emergency cuts in late May/early June 2023

actions.description: EVN applied rolling and sometimes unannounced cuts to homes and businesses in Hanoi and northern provinces; peak daily shedding reached about 5,000 MW and fell to 2,000-2,500 MW by mid-June. Industrial parks had scheduled cuts, e.g. 5am-5pm.
actions.lead_time_basis: cuts began within weeks of reservoirs reaching dead level
actions.cost_note: Economic cost captured in World Bank USD 1.4bn estimate
actions.effect: Balanced a supply deficit; peak shedding about 5,000 MW, reduced to 2,000-2,500 MW as inflows improved

actions.description: Provinces such as Bac Giang cut household power from 6 June to prioritise supply to major factories; government directed priority for large industrial users.
actions.lead_time_basis: same-month decision and application
actions.effect: Not quantified; businesses still reported revenue losses up to 10%

actions.description: EVN and the Ministry of Industry and Trade asked households and businesses to conserve; Hanoi switched off decorative and part of street lighting (Hoan Kiem Lake lights off at 7-8pm, 50% of Long Bien Bridge lights off); firms shifted production to off-peak/night hours.
actions.lead_time_basis: announced as shortages emerged late May/early June
actions.effect: Not quantified

actions.description: Electricity imports from China and Laos into the northern grid.
actions.lead_time_basis: no decision date found
actions.effect: 10-12 GWh/day, only 2.7% of northern daily demand of 445-450 GWh

actions.description: Structural response: 500kV circuit 3 transmission line Quang Trach-Pho Noi (519 km, four sub-projects) built on an accelerated schedule to raise North Central-to-North transfer capacity.
actions.lead_time_basis: June 2023 crisis to energisation on 27 Aug 2024; construction started 18 Jan 2024 (about 7 months of construction)
actions.cost_note: About VND 22 trillion (~USD 916m as reported by VnEconomy; other reports say ~VND 23 trillion)
actions.effect: Transfer capacity to the north raised from 2,200 MW to about 5,000 MW (over 20 TWh/yr deliverable)

outcome.blackout_or_shedding: Rolling cuts across northern Vietnam late May-22 June 2023; one reported outage lasted 26 hours; peak load shed ~5,000 MW
outcome.shedding_hours_note: 12 h (5am-5pm) scheduled industrial-park cut; isolated outages longer
outcome.gdp_impact: About USD 1.4bn, ~0.3% of GDP (World Bank preliminary estimate, Aug 2023); surveyed northern firms lost up to 10% of revenue; peak supply deficit 1.8 GW per World Bank

demos.name: Zambia + Zimbabwe (Kariba, 2027)
demos.hydro_share_note: Zambia 86.2% (countries.json); Zimbabwe 55.6%. Zambia used for matching.
demos.storage_note: Kariba: 64.8 BCM usable, multi-year storage (kariba.json storage_curve).
demos.imports_note: Analyst label: SAPP links via Mozambique (HCB), South Africa, Namibia, Botswana; in 2024 imports covered a small part of the deficit and were costly (see ZMB-ZWE-2024 case).
demos.warning_lead_note: Analyst estimate: ZRA already cut the 2027 allocation to 23 BCM (-36%, kariba.json zra_projection) and projects 9% usable at end-2027. If the 2026-27 rains fail under the El Nino, the deepest shortfall is in the second half of 2027, 9+ months away.
demos.risk_summary: Kariba 31.7% usable (ZRA gauge 2026-11-10). ZRA: 2027 allocation 23 BCM (2026: 36 BCM), end-2027 projection 9% usable. Patronus Dec-2027 median 31% usable, P10 0%, 36% of El Nino members end 2027 below 9%. ENSO: El Nino loser (Kariba level change -87% vs neutral years, p = 0.04).
demos.takeaway: About 9 months of lead puts Kariba in the 6+ month window, which neither 2015 nor 2024 had. The cases point to four steps. (1) Enforce the 23 BCM allocation, since both earlier cuts were overdrawn. (2) Contract imports and rentals now, competitively: 2015 imports cost USD 183/MWh against 5 USc/kWh retail, and in 2024 the first 12 MW of rental arrived only in Aug. (3) If the deficit is large, prefer quotas with bonus/penalty (Brazil 2001: -16.7%, no blackouts) and a paid savings campaign (Colombia 2016) over 20 h/day rotational cuts. (4) Protect water pumping and hospitals. Watch ZESCO debt and avoid take-or-pay lock-in (Ghana 2015).

similar_cases.what_worked: Individual quotas with price incentives, heavy media repetition and a fixed known end date produced a fast cut of about 20% without blackouts. Allowance trading let energy shift to the industries that valued it most. Household efficiency gains persisted for years.
similar_cases.what_failed: Rules were complex and changed several times. Fines could not fund bonuses. Utilities lacked staff for cut-offs, and Rio de Janeiro banned them. Emergency thermal contracts came late and left consumers with long-lived charges. Underlying causes were investment lagging demand and weak transmission between subsystems.

similar_cases.what_worked: The reliability-charge capacity market secured thermal backup. Apagar Paga's symmetric bonus/penalty plus strong communication produced savings far above target within weeks. Ecuador imports, LNG and coordination with the IDEAM met agency also helped. Fedesarrollo credits the post-1994 reforms with avoiding rationing.
similar_cases.what_failed: The campaign launched late (March 2016). The scarcity-price formula was tied to oil prices, so after the oil crash generators produced at a loss. Government was slow to resolve the price issue, thermal plants failed operationally, and there was no contingency for the Guatape fire, which took about 4% of national capacity offline. Guatape was not expected back at full output until Sep 2017.

similar_cases.what_worked: Very large reservoir storage plus import capacity gave time; saving water over the summer and the threat of export controls kept reservoirs from running out before spring.
similar_cases.what_failed: The price spike passed straight to consumers in the south, and an expensive universal subsidy (about NOK 32.6 bn in 2022) followed; the export-control idea caused friction with neighbours.

limits: Case evidence, not causal proof. The cases show what was done and what followed; rain, the economy and other measures changed at the same time, so no single action's effect is isolated.
Costs vary by country and year (fuel prices, currency, contract terms). Costs here are as reported in the cited source and year; they are not comparable to the cent.
Survivorship and documentation bias: well-documented crises (Brazil, Ecuador, Zambia) are over-represented; quiet successes are under-reported.
Lead times are partly estimated (decision date to first effect, from news dates) and marked as estimates where so.
The matching fields for storage type and import strength are analyst labels, not measured; similarity is a simple weighted rule, not a trained model.
Patronus does not prescribe policy. It shows options with the evidence and the trade-offs (debt, fossil lock-in, equity). Decisions belong to ministries, regulators and utilities.

Bucket = how far ahead of the expected shortfall an action must start to matter, not how long the paperwork takes.

evidence_strength is computed from the cases: strong = quantified effect in >= 3 cases; moderate = quantified in 2 cases, or in 1 case and used in >= 3; weak = quantified in 1 case; unmeasured = used but no case measured an effect. It counts documented use, not proof of effect.
Post-crisis bill compensation (Ecuador 2010) is recorded in the case but is not a remediation option.
'Measured' means a case reported a number for the action's effect, including measured failures (e.g. Kariba allocations overdrawn by 39%). Read the evidence_summary for direction.
